transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's a burning when I pass water, and I'm needing to go much more often than usual. It's been going on for a little while now and it's getting rather tiresome.
Do you have any allergies, or have you ever had a bad reaction to a medicine?
Yes, I'm allergic to an antibiotic called trimethoprim — it gave me an itchy rash once.
How much is this affecting your daily life?
I've stopped going to the residents' coffee morning, because I'm worried I won't reach a toilet in time.
Could you tell me what medicines you take regularly, including any that have been started or changed recently, and the dose if you know it?

I take a tablet for my underactive thyroid each morning, and one for my thin bones once a week. I also use a cream from the hospital twice a week, but I can't for the life of me remember what it's called.
Would you say these symptoms bother you a little, a moderate amount, or a lot — or you're not sure?
It's uncomfortable, but I'd say it's moderate — I'm managing, it's not unbearable.
Have you noticed any other symptoms along with the burning when you pass water and needing to go more often?
The water looks cloudy and smells stronger than usual. I haven't seen any blood, though.
Whereabouts do you feel the burning when you pass water?
It's just down below, when the water comes out. I haven't noticed it anywhere else.
Have you noticed anything at all that seems to make the burning better or worse?
I can't say I've noticed anything that makes it better or worse. It's just there each time I go.
You've mentioned an underactive thyroid and thin bones — is there anything else about your past health that you'd like to add?
I had a water infection about a year ago, and they gave me antibiotics for it. That's the only other thing I can think of.
When did you first start noticing the burning and needing to go more often?
It came on a few days back — I couldn't tell you the exact day.
Have you noticed anything else going on, besides the burning, needing to go more often, and the cloudy, strong-smelling urine?
No, nothing like that — no fever, no shivers, no back or side pain, and I haven't been sick. My niece says she hasn't noticed me being confused either.
Which of these fits best for you just now: you're taking medicines you've been on for a while, you've recently started something new or had a change to one, or you're not sure?
They're all things I've been on for a good while — nothing new has been started or changed lately, as far as I know.
Is there anything else you take for your health that we haven't talked about yet — even something you only use now and then?
No, just the cream I mentioned, and the two tablets. I can't think of anything else.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
